title: Choose the new visual world
question: A full restart, playful and reactive. The roll dealt the pop-up book. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Pop-up Bush Picture Book
options.lineage: Australian picture books and paper-engineered pop-ups
options.thesis: The rescue told as a pop-up book you play with: open it and the grass tree springs up out of the gutter.
materials: die-cut card in flat gouache colour
real Replants photos tipped in like snapshots
options.viewport: A 3D pop-up spread fills the screen. The grass tree folds up as the page opens; pulling the paper tab grows it, and the price flap flips to the new figure. Book it from the same spread.
options.risk: Reads as a children's book unless the type, prices and booking stay plain and grown-up.

raised.raise: One line of travel: the page follows the rescue, bush to crane truck to your garden, and the truck drives across each spread as you scroll.
The bush keeps Perth time: the paper sky is dawn, noon or dusk by the visitor's own clock.
Every tipped-in photo carries its origin beside it, such as Mahogany Creek or a Fremantle install.
One colour is reserved for the action: only the booking controls wear it.
Every tab, wheel and flap moves on damped springs and overshoots a little, never snaps.

options.label: After the Fire
options.lineage: WA bush regrowth after a burn
options.thesis: Grass trees are fire trees: a black trunk, a bright green crown, and the flower spike that follows a burn.
options.viewport: A huge 3D blackened trunk and crown fill the screen. Embers drift up and swirl around the cursor, and the size picker sits on an ash panel.
options.risk: Near-black with one hot accent is where many sites land, and fire imagery can unsettle buyers in a bushfire state.

options.label: Rainbow Skirt Poster
options.thesis: Each section is one poster: a jet-black grass-tree silhouette whose skirt unfurls in ribbons of flat candy colour.
options.viewport: A giant silhouette anchors the screen. Its skirt ribbons sway and part around the cursor, and the size and price sit in a lettered frame below.
options.case: Fuses well: a grass tree's skirt reads as the poster's ribboned hair, which gives clear emblems. It loses on audience fit, because it is American 60s pop rather than WA.
options.risk: Becomes a psychedelic costume if the ribbons aren't also the controls.

options.label: Agit-train Broadside
options.thesis: The rescue as a campaign train of red wedges and stencilled slogans.
options.viewport: Railcars of slogans and photos driving across the screen on one diagonal.
options.case: Fuses poorly: Perth gardeners don't see themselves in Soviet propaganda, and the slogans crowd out prices.
options.kept: One strong line of travel that scroll drives.

options.label: Sleeping City Fold
options.thesis: Suburbs folding like a quilt at night.
options.viewport: A night map that folds over the bush.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dream logic hides the size, price and booking.
options.kept: The scene follows the visitor's real local time.

options.label: Memory Quilt Atlas
options.thesis: Each rescue as one stitched patch with its own history.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it is sombre and slow, and the visitor wants a tree, not an archive.

options.label: Arcade Pixel Glow
options.thesis: The rescue as a pixel game.
options.viewport: A pixel bush you dig trees out of.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an older audience, and pixel type fails the large-text rule.
options.kept: One colour reserved by law for the action.

options.label: Night-flight Gauges
options.thesis: Tree health as six glowing dials.
options.viewport: Six gauges for size, price, age and care.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a cockpit is a tool costume, nothing a gardener knows.
options.kept: Damped physical motion on every control.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A garden-centre shop, done impeccably: photo hero, product grid, add to cart.
canonCard.viewport: A big photo of an installed grass tree, a headline and a shop button, then a grid of sizes with prices.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every nursery by design.
